pricing.metaTitle: Wi-Mall pricing — start free, pay when it pays you back
pricing.metaDescription: What Wi-Mall costs for vendors, delivery agencies and delivery agents. Free tiers that never expire, vendor plans from 5,000 FCFA per 30 days, commission from 7% down to 3%, and nothing that renews itself.
pricing.title: Start at zero. Pay when it pays you back.
pricing.lead: Vendors, delivery agencies and delivery agents each get a free tier that never expires. Paid plans raise your limits and, for vendors, cut the commission on every order. No setup fee, no contract, and nothing renews itself.

howWeEarn.title: How Wi-Mall makes money
howWeEarn.lead: Worth stating plainly, because it is what decides whether this arrangement works for you.

commission.title: A commission on each paid order
commission.body: A percentage of the order total, taken at the moment the customer pays. The vendor's plan sets it: 7% on the free tier, 5% on Growth, 3% on Business.

plans.title: Optional plan subscriptions
plans.body: A 30-day term that raises your limits. Every role can operate indefinitely without ever buying one.

credits.title: Credits for metered work
credits.body: Indexing a product so the AI can recommend it, and sending a billable WhatsApp template message. Your plan includes an allowance; top up only if you use it all.

delivery.title: Nothing out of the delivery fee
delivery.body: The delivery fee is set by the delivery agency and divided between that agency and the agent who ran the delivery. Wi-Mall takes no share of it.

howWeEarn.customerNote: Customers pay for what they buy and nothing else. There is no fee, no subscription and no account charge for shopping on Wi-Mall.

vendor.title: Vendor plans
vendor.lead: The commission is the number worth comparing. On a month of 400,000 FCFA in paid orders, moving from Starter to Growth saves 8,000 FCFA in commission and costs 5,000.
vendor.note: Limits count published products. At the cap, creating another is refused until you deactivate one or move up a tier — nothing already published is taken down.

agency.title: Delivery agency plans
agency.lead: An agency's limit is how many shipments can be open at the same time, not how many you run in a month. Finish a delivery and the slot frees up.
agency.note: This cap is soft. Cross it and you get an alert, not a stop — deliveries keep flowing while you decide whether to move up.

agent.title: Delivery agent plans
agent.lead: Same idea as agencies: the number is how many deliveries you can be holding at any one moment, not a monthly quota.
agent.note: This cap is hard. Accepting one more offer past your ceiling is refused until one of the deliveries you are holding is finished.

credits.title: What credits are
credits.p1: Two things on Wi-Mall cost real money every time they happen, so they are metered rather than bundled: indexing one of your products so the AI assistant can find and recommend it, and sending one billable WhatsApp template message to a customer. Each costs 1 credit.
credits.p2: Activating a plan grants its allowance once — 50 credits on the vendor free tier, 4,500 on Business. If you use it all, top up in packs. The larger the pack, the less each credit costs.
credits.packsCaption: Credit top-up packs and their prices

payment.title: How paying works
payment.p1: Plans and credit packs are paid through NotchPay or MyCoolPay for mobile money, or Stripe for cards. Nothing is stored and charged again later — there is no recurring subscription anywhere on Wi-Mall.
payment.p2: A paid term simply runs out after 30 days. If you bought another plan while one was still running, it was queued and takes over at that moment; if you did not, you drop back to your role's free tier and carry on working. You can hold one active plan and one queued plan at a time.
payment.p3: If a card payment is reversed after the fact, the plan it bought rolls back to the free tier and any credits it granted are taken back — which can leave a balance negative until it is topped up.

cta.title: The free tier needs no payment method
cta.body: Set your catalogue up, see what sells, and move up a tier only when the commission maths says you should.
cta.finePrint: Free tiers never expire. Paid terms run 30 days and do not auto-renew.

pricing.unsoldTierNote: Tiers marked as not on sale are listed at their catalogue price but cannot be bought here today. The free tier is always available.

vendors.metaTitle: Sell on WhatsApp without a website — Wi-Mall for vendors
vendors.metaDescription: Upload your products once and let Wi-Mall's AI assistant sell them inside WhatsApp. No storefront, no app, no developer. Free tier: 15 products, 7% commission, no expiry.
vendors.title: Sell on WhatsApp without a website
vendors.lead: You do not need a storefront, a domain or a developer. Upload your products once, and Wi-Mall's AI assistant sells them inside the WhatsApp conversations your customers are already having.

problem.title: You already sell on WhatsApp. That is the problem.
problem.p1: The conversation itself works. People trust it, it costs almost nothing in data to open, and nobody has to create an account to talk to you. What does not work is that you are the catalogue, the salesperson and the dispatcher — and all three only exist while your phone is in your hand.
problem.p2: So the same five questions come back all day. Is it still available. How much. What colours. Do you deliver to my area. Can I pay when it arrives. Miss an hour and you have missed the sale, because the customer has already asked somebody else.
problem.p3: Wi-Mall does not move you off WhatsApp. It puts a real catalogue and an assistant behind the chat, so those five questions get answered at two in the morning the same way they would be answered at two in the afternoon.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Six steps, and you are only involved in the first and the last.
how.s1Body: Photos, prices, descriptions, variants and stock. Simple products, products with options, digital downloads and bookable services all work.
how.s2Body: Each one is indexed so the assistant can match it to what a customer describes, rather than only to the exact words they typed.
how.s3Body: They say what they are looking for in their own words. The assistant answers with your products and your stock, not with generic advice.
how.s4Title: The order is created in the chat
how.s4Body: The customer confirms and pays without leaving WhatsApp — mobile money, card, or cash when it arrives.
how.s5Body: The order becomes a shipment, an agency dispatches one of its agents, and the customer can follow where it is.
how.s6Title: Your share is recorded and paid
how.s6Body: The order total, minus the platform commission and the delivery fee, lands in your earnings with every part of the split written down.

included.title: What you get
included.i1: A product catalogue with variants, options, stock levels and per-product shipping rules
included.i2: An AI assistant that answers in the customer's language, at any hour
included.i3: Orders with a real lifecycle, instead of a chat thread you have to re-read
included.i4: Delivery through the agencies already on the platform, so you never have to own a bike
included.i5: Digital products and bookable services alongside physical goods
included.i6: An earnings ledger showing commission, delivery fee and your net on every single order
included.i7: Analytics on what sells, and stock requests for what runs out
included.i8: Notifications in the dashboard, by push, by email, on Telegram and on WhatsApp

cost.title: What it costs
cost.p1: The free tier is not a trial. Starter lets you publish 15 products with 1 GB of media, takes 7% of each paid order, and never expires.
cost.p2: Growth is 5,000 FCFA per 30 days: 150 products, 10 GB, and the commission drops to 5%. Business is 25,000 FCFA per 30 days for unlimited products, 100 GB and 3%. Nothing renews on its own — when a term ends you either move to the plan you queued, or go back to Starter and keep selling.

start.title: What you need to start
start.lead: Setup is four steps and only the first is required. You can be listing products before you have decided on branding or delivery policy.
start.i1: A WhatsApp number you can verify
start.i2: Your country and a way to be paid out — that is the whole of the required step
start.i3: Products with a photo, a price and a short description
start.i4: Optionally: a delivery agency to link with, your branding, and your own return and shipping policy

cta.title: Put your catalogue where the conversation already is
cta.body: Starter costs nothing, needs no payment method, and does not expire. If it works, the paid tiers pay for themselves in commission.
cta.finePrint: 15 products, 1 GB and 7% commission on the free tier. No card required.

agencies.metaTitle: Delivery agencies on Wi-Mall — orders that arrive paid and addressed
agencies.metaDescription: Run a delivery business on Wi-Mall: paid orders dispatched to your agents, coverage by region, live tracking, cash-on-delivery reconciliation. You set the delivery fee and Wi-Mall takes none of it.
agencies.title: Orders that arrive already paid and already addressed
agencies.lead: Wi-Mall hands your agency real shipments with a destination and a fee attached. You dispatch them to your agents, your agents deliver, and the delivery fee is yours to split — Wi-Mall takes no part of it.

money.title: Where an agency's money comes from
money.p1: You set your own delivery pricing in your agency policy. When an order is paid, the fee for each of its shipments is reserved against that shipment and taken out of the vendor's side of the order — not added on top of what you are owed.
money.p2: When a delivery finishes, that reserved fee is divided between your agency and the agent who ran it, following the contract you agreed with that agent: either a percentage of the fee, or a flat amount per delivery. Whatever is left after the agent's cut is your agency's.
money.p3: Wi-Mall's commission comes out of the vendor's share of the order total. It never touches the delivery fee. If a shipment has no agent contract attached, the agency keeps the whole fee.
money.codNote: Cash on delivery is handled as its own flow: the agent collects, the collection is recorded against the agency, and the same split runs on the cash instead of on the card payment.

run.title: What you actually run
run.i1Body: Approach agents or accept the ones who apply. Every relationship is its own contract, with its own status, fee split and cash allocation.
run.i2Body: Your agency registers a country and the regions it covers. Cameroon's ten are all available; orders outside them are not routed to you.
run.i3Body: Send an offer to the agent you choose, or let assignment route it to the nearest available one and take the first acceptance.
run.i4Body: Follow a delivery while it runs, and let the customer follow it too. Enabled on every plan tier, including the free one.
run.i5Body: Cash-on-delivery collections are tracked per agent and reconciled against what has been handed over, with a handling fee of your own.
run.i6Body: A ledger for every shipment: what the fee was, what the agent took, what you kept, and what happened when a delivery came back.

capacity.title: Capacity, and what happens at the limit
capacity.p1: The free tier lets you hold 1,000 shipments open at the same time. That is a working ceiling, not a monthly quota — every completed delivery frees its slot back up.
capacity.p2: The cap is deliberately soft. If you cross it, you get an alert and the option to move up; nothing about checkout, dispatch or delivery stops working. An agency that is at capacity is having a good week, and the platform should not punish that.

start.title: What you need to register
start.i1: A WhatsApp number you can verify
start.i2: At least one headquarters address, and the regions you intend to cover
start.i4: Your delivery policy — the pricing you charge and the terms you deliver under

cta.title: Bring your fleet the orders
cta.body: Registering costs nothing and the free tier carries a thousand open deliveries. The only thing you need decided before you start is what you charge.
cta.finePrint: Free tier: 1,000 open shipments, 5 GB, live tracking included.

agents.metaDescription: Deliver for Wi-Mall on your own schedule. Sign up independently, join one agency or several, see what a run pays before you accept it, and get your share of every delivery fee.
agents.title: Deliver on your own terms. See the pay before you accept.
agents.lead: Sign up as a delivery agent, join an agency — or several — and start receiving delivery offers on your phone. Every offer tells you what the run pays before you decide.

how.title: How it works
how.s1Body: You register independently and are attached to no agency at first. Your account, your details, your vehicle.
how.s2Body: Apply to one, or accept an agency that approaches you. You can hold contracts with several at the same time.
how.s3Body: A delivery arrives on your phone with pickup, drop-off and what it pays. Accept it, or leave it for someone else.
how.s4Body: Collect from the vendor, deliver to the customer, and confirm it with proof of delivery.
how.s5Title: Collect the cash if it is a COD run
how.s5Body: For cash-on-delivery orders you collect at the door and hand it over to your agency, tracked against your name.
how.s6Body: Your cut of the delivery fee is allocated to you when the run is completed, at the split your contract sets.

earnings.title: What you earn
earnings.p1: Your earnings come out of the delivery fee on each shipment. How much of it is yours is set in the contract you hold with that agency: either a percentage of the fee, or a flat amount per delivery.
earnings.p2: Because it is per contract, two agencies can pay differently for the same kind of run — and you can see what a specific job pays before accepting it rather than after. A delivery that ends in a return is settled under its own rule rather than being written off.
earnings.p3: Wi-Mall takes nothing from the delivery fee. The whole of it is divided between your agency and you.

capacity.title: How many at once
capacity.p1: The free tier lets you hold 20 deliveries at the same time. Finish one and the slot comes back.
capacity.p2: Unlike the agency cap, this one is firm: accepting an offer beyond your ceiling is refused rather than merely flagged. The point is that a customer waiting on a delivery you cannot get to is worse than an offer you did not receive.

start.title: What you need
start.i1: A smartphone and a WhatsApp number you can verify
start.i2: A vehicle — bike, car, van or truck — with its type and colour on your profile
start.i3: An agency to hold a contract with, which you can apply to after signing up
start.i4: Optionally an emergency contact, and a photo of the vehicle

cta.title: Start with one agency, or five
cta.body: Signing up is free and independent. Nothing obliges you to a single agency, and no offer is binding until you accept it.
cta.finePrint: Free tier: 20 deliveries held at once. No monthly quota.

customers.metaTitle: Shop on WhatsApp — Wi-Mall for customers
customers.metaDescription: Buy from local vendors inside a WhatsApp conversation. No app to install and no account to create: describe what you want, get real products at real prices, pay by mobile money, card or cash on delivery, and have it brought to your door.
customers.title: Shopping is a conversation. There is nothing to install.
customers.lead: Open WhatsApp, say what you are looking for, and an assistant answers with real products from real vendors. You order and pay in the same thread, and a delivery agent brings it to you.

problem.title: Why buying works this way
problem.p1: Most of the shops worth buying from here have no website. They have a WhatsApp number, a few photos and someone answering messages between other jobs. Buying means asking whether an item is still available, waiting for the reply, agreeing a price, and then arranging delivery in a separate conversation.
problem.p2: The usual fix is an app: a download, an account, a password and a card form — a lot of steps to buy a phone charger, over a connection that may not survive them.
problem.p3: Wi-Mall keeps the conversation and takes out the waiting. Behind the chat is a real catalogue: vendors keep their stock and their prices current in their own dashboard, so what the assistant quotes you is what the vendor is selling today.

how.title: How buying works
how.lead: Six steps, all of them inside one chat.
how.s1Body: Tap the WhatsApp link, or save the Wi-Mall number and message it. There is no sign-up screen — the number you are writing from is your identity.
how.s2Body: Write it the way you would say it to a friend: “wireless earbuds under 15,000 FCFA”, “a school bag for a six-year-old”. The assistant reads your language and replies in it.
how.s3Body: You get real products with photos, prices and whether they are in stock. Ask about a specific one — size, colour, battery, warranty — and the answer is about that product, not a brochure.
how.s4Body: Once you have chosen, the order is created in the conversation. You confirm the quantity and the address, and you see the delivery fee before anything is charged.
how.s5Title: Pay the way you already pay
how.s5Body: Mobile money, card, or cash handed to the agent at the door where the vendor and the agency accept it.
how.s6Body: The vendor packs it, a delivery agency takes it on and one of its agents brings it to you. The updates arrive in the thread you ordered in.

ask.title: What you can ask for
ask.lead: The assistant is there to be talked to, not searched. Everything on this list is a normal message to send it.
ask.i1: Describe a product instead of knowing what it is called
ask.i2: Set a budget and only be shown what fits inside it
ask.i3: Ask about one item — size, colour, condition, what is in the box
ask.i4: Compare two of the products it has just shown you
ask.i5: Ask what delivery to your area costs and how long it takes
ask.i6: Change the quantity or the address before you confirm
ask.i7: Ask where an order has got to after you have paid for it
ask.i8: Write in French, English, Portuguese, Spanish or Arabic

pay.title: How you pay
pay.lead: All three run through the same conversation. Which ones a given order offers depends on the vendor and, for cash, on the agency delivering it.
pay.mobileBody: MTN, Orange and Moov, through NotchPay or MyCoolPay. You approve it on your own phone, as you would any other transfer.
pay.cardBody: Visa and Mastercard through Stripe, for anyone who would rather pay that way or is paying from abroad.
pay.codBody: Hand the money to the agent at the door. Here that is a first-class way to pay rather than an exception, and the collection is recorded against the agent who took it.

delivery.title: Getting it to you
delivery.p1: Deliveries are handled by local agencies and the agents who work with them, not by Wi-Mall itself. An agency registers the regions it covers, so whether an order can reach you depends on an agency working where you are.
delivery.p2: The delivery fee is set by the vendor and shown to you before you confirm, not added at the end. Where a vendor delivers free, you see that in the same place.
delivery.p3: Cameroon is the first market. All ten regions can be covered, and the cities with the most vendors and agencies today are Douala, Yaoundé, Bafoussam, Bamenda and Garoua.

cost.title: What it costs you
cost.p1: Nothing. There is no platform fee for buying, no subscription and no account to pay for. You pay the vendor for the product, and the delivery fee where one applies.
cost.p2: The money comes from the selling side instead: vendors pay for their plan and a commission on what they sell. It is worth knowing, because it is the reason nobody is trying to charge you for the conversation.

need.i2: An address, or a landmark an agent can actually find
need.i3: Mobile money, a card, or cash for the agent at the door

faq.metaTitle: Wi-Mall FAQ — selling, delivering and paying on WhatsApp
faq.metaDescription: Straight answers about Wi-Mall: how buying on WhatsApp works, what selling costs, how delivery agencies and agents are paid, which payment methods work, and where the platform operates.
faq.title: Questions, answered plainly
faq.lead: If something here is out of date or missing, the honest answer is usually in the product itself — but these are the questions people actually ask before they sign up.

whatIsWiMall.a: A commerce platform that runs inside WhatsApp. Vendors upload a catalogue; customers chat with an AI assistant that understands what they are looking for, recommends products and creates the order in the conversation; delivery agencies and their agents deliver it. Nobody involved needs a website or an app.

howShopping.a: You open a WhatsApp conversation and describe what you want in your own words. The assistant answers with real products from real vendors, along with prices and availability, and can answer follow-up questions about them. When you are ready it creates the order and takes payment in the same thread.

needApp.q: Do I need to download an app or make an account?
needApp.a: Not as a customer. Buying happens in WhatsApp, which you already have. Vendors, delivery agencies and agents do have accounts, because they need dashboards — but customers do not.

whereAvailable.a: Cameroon first. All ten regions are available for a delivery agency to register coverage in, and delivery in any given place depends on an agency covering that region. Prices are in FCFA and the platform is built around the payment methods used there.

languages.q: What languages does Wi-Mall work in?
languages.a: The site and the product are in French, English, Portuguese, Spanish and Arabic, with right-to-left layout for Arabic. For Cameroon the two that matter most are French and English, and the assistant answers a customer in the language they wrote in.

shopperCost.q: Does it cost anything to shop on Wi-Mall?
shopperCost.a: No. Customers pay for what they buy and for delivery where the vendor charges it. There is no platform fee, no subscription and no account charge on the buying side.

vendorStart.q: What do I need to start selling?
vendorStart.a: A WhatsApp number you can verify, your country, and a way to be paid out. That is the only required setup step. Linking a delivery agency, adding branding and writing your own policies are all optional and can be done later.

vendorWebsite.q: Do I need a website or an online shop?
vendorWebsite.a: No, and that is the point. Your catalogue lives on Wi-Mall and is sold through the WhatsApp conversation. There is no storefront to design, no domain to buy and no developer to pay.

vendorCost.a: The Starter tier is free and never expires: 15 published products, 1 GB of media, and 7% commission on each paid order. Growth is 5,000 FCFA per 30 days for 150 products and 5% commission; Business is 25,000 FCFA per 30 days for unlimited products and 3%.

vendorProductLimit.q: What happens when I reach my product limit?
vendorProductLimit.a: Creating another product is refused until you either deactivate one you no longer sell or move up a tier. Nothing already published is removed, and no order in flight is affected.

vendorDigital.q: Can I sell digital products or services?
vendorDigital.a: Yes. Alongside physical goods you can sell digital downloads, and bookable services with their own availability rules and calendar. Digital orders have no shipment, so there is no delivery fee on them.

vendorDelivery.q: Do I have to handle delivery myself?
vendorDelivery.a: No. Delivery is run by the agencies on the platform. A paid order becomes a shipment, an agency dispatches one of its agents, and the delivery fee is taken from the order and split between that agency and the agent. You can link with a specific agency, or let the platform route it.

vendorPayout.a: Your net on an order is held the moment the customer's payment settles. It becomes withdrawable once the order completes — the customer confirms delivery, or it auto-confirms seven days after delivery — plus a seven-day hold window after that. From there you request a payout of your available balance. The ledger shows the gross, the commission, the delivery fee and your net for every order, so the figure is never a mystery.

agencyEarn.q: How does a delivery agency make money?
agencyEarn.a: From the delivery fee, which you set yourself in your agency policy. It is reserved against each shipment when the order is paid and divided when the delivery completes: the agent takes the cut their contract specifies, and your agency keeps the rest. Wi-Mall takes no share of the delivery fee.

agencyCoverage.q: How do I choose where my agency delivers?
agencyCoverage.a: By region. Your agency registers a country and then selects the regions it covers — Cameroon has ten, from Littoral and Centre to the Far North. Orders outside your coverage are not routed to you.

agencySoftCap.q: What happens if my agency hits its shipment limit?
agencySoftCap.a: Nothing stops. The agency cap is soft on purpose: crossing it raises an alert and suggests moving up a tier, but checkout, dispatch and delivery all keep working. Every completed delivery frees a slot back up.

agentEarn.q: How much does an agent earn per delivery?
agentEarn.a: It depends on the contract you hold with the agency: either a percentage of that shipment's delivery fee, or a flat amount per delivery. You can see what a specific job pays before you accept it, and holding contracts with several agencies at once is normal.

agentJoin.q: Can I work as an agent without joining an agency?
agentJoin.a: You sign up on your own and belong to no agency at first, but deliveries reach you through an agency contract. You can apply to an agency, or accept one that approaches you — and you can hold several contracts at the same time.

agentCapacity.q: How many deliveries can I hold at once?
agentCapacity.a: Twenty on the free tier. Unlike the agency limit this one is enforced: accepting an offer past your ceiling is refused until one of the deliveries you are already holding is completed.

paymentMethods.a: Mobile money through NotchPay or MyCoolPay, covering MTN, Orange and Moov; cards through Stripe; and cash on delivery where the vendor and agency accept it.

cashOnDelivery.a: Yes, and it is treated as a first-class flow rather than an exception. The agent collects at the door, the collection is recorded against them and reconciled with their agency, and everybody's share is split from the cash the same way it would be from a card payment.

credits.q: What are credits, and do I have to buy them?
credits.a: Credits meter two things that cost money every time they happen: indexing a product so the assistant can recommend it, and sending a billable WhatsApp template message. Each costs one credit. Every plan grants an allowance when it activates, so most accounts never buy any; if you use yours up, packs start at 600 FCFA for 100 credits.

renewal.a: No. There is no stored card and no recurring charge anywhere on Wi-Mall. A paid plan runs its 30 days and then either hands over to a plan you queued while it was running, or drops you back to your role's free tier.

downgrade.q: What happens if I stop paying?
downgrade.a: You go back to the free tier of your role and carry on working with its limits. Nothing is deleted and no account is closed. If a card payment is reversed after the fact, the plan it bought is rolled back and the credits it granted are taken back with it.

cta.title: Still deciding?
cta.body: Every role has a free tier that never expires, so the cheapest way to answer a question about Wi-Mall is usually to try it.
cta.finePrint: No payment method required to start.

country.metaTitle: Wi-Mall in Cameroon — WhatsApp commerce in FCFA
country.metaDescription: Wi-Mall is built for Cameroon first: prices in FCFA, French and English, MTN and Orange mobile money, cash on delivery, and delivery coverage across all ten regions.
country.title: Built for Cameroon first
country.lead: Not a Western storefront translated into French. Wi-Mall prices in FCFA, speaks French and English, settles through the mobile money people actually use, and organises delivery by region — because that is how the country is organised.

why.title: Why here first
why.p1: Commerce in Cameroon already happens in WhatsApp. A seller posts to a status, a buyer replies, they negotiate in the thread, and somebody arranges a moto. None of that needs to be replaced — it needs a catalogue behind it, a way to take payment that both sides trust, and a delivery leg that does not depend on knowing a guy.
why.p2: That is the whole design. The assistant sells from a real catalogue inside the conversation the customer was already going to have. Payment goes through the mobile money accounts that most adults already hold. Delivery goes to an agency that registered the regions it covers, and to an agent who gets paid per run.
why.p3: It also means the constraints are the design brief, not an afterthought: entry-level phones, expensive data, and networks that drop. The product is built to keep working through all three.

coverage.title: Where deliveries can run
coverage.lead: Delivery coverage follows the agencies on the platform. An agency registers a country and the regions it covers, and all ten of Cameroon's regions are available to register.
coverage.note: A region with no agency covering it yet is not a region Wi-Mall refuses — it is one where an agency has not registered. If you run deliveries there, that is an opening rather than an obstacle.

payments.title: Paying, the way it is actually done here

city.sellingP1: The setup is the same everywhere: upload a catalogue, and the assistant sells from it inside WhatsApp. What changes by city is who is buying and how far a delivery has to travel — and both of those are decided by the agencies covering the region rather than by us.

douala.lead: Douala is where most of the country's goods arrive and most of its trade is settled — which makes it the hardest place to be a small seller and the best place to have someone else handle discovery and delivery.
douala.context: The port city and economic capital of Cameroon, in the Littoral region. Commerce concentrates around Marché Mboppi and the Marché Central, with business districts in Akwa and Bonanjo, dense residential trade through New Bell and Deido, and a whole second half of the city across the Wouri in Bonabéri.
douala.angle: Distance is the real cost here. A customer in Bonabéri and a seller in Akwa are twenty minutes apart on a good day and an hour on a bad one, so the delivery leg is worth organising properly rather than improvising per order.

yaounde.lead: Yaoundé buys differently from Douala: more salaried, more administrative, more predictable in when it orders and where it wants things delivered.
yaounde.context: The political capital, in the Centre region, spread over its hills. Trade concentrates at Marché Mokolo and Marché Mfoundi, with commercial density through Mvog-Mbi and Nlongkak and a well-off residential market in Bastos.
yaounde.angle: The hills make routing matter more than raw distance — two neighbourhoods can be close on a map and far apart in practice. An agency that knows the city's actual routes is worth more here than one that only knows its addresses.

bafoussam.lead: Bafoussam sits at the centre of a trading region rather than at the end of one, which changes what a seller there can reach.
bafoussam.context: Capital of the West region and the commercial hub of the Grassfields, with a market that draws from Dschang, Mbouda, Bafang and Foumban. Agricultural trade and the region's long merchant tradition give it a density of small businesses out of proportion to its size.
bafoussam.angle: The opportunity is regional, not municipal. A vendor in Bafoussam whose catalogue is discoverable can sell into the surrounding towns, and an agency covering the West region can serve all of them from one base.

bamenda.lead: Bamenda is the largest Anglophone market in the country, and it is served far worse than its size deserves by platforms that launch in French only.
bamenda.context: Capital of the Northwest region, high in the Grassfields, with commerce centred on the Bamenda Main Market and Nkwen. It anchors a wider English-speaking trade area that reaches Kumbo, Bali and Ndop.
bamenda.angle: Language is the practical difference here. Wi-Mall's assistant answers in the language the customer writes in, so a seller in Bamenda is not asking their customers to switch into French to buy something.

garoua.lead: Garoua trades north and across borders as much as it trades with the south, and the distances involved make organised delivery worth more, not less.
garoua.context: Capital of the North region on the Bénoué river, historically a river port and still the commercial centre for a large, thinly populated area that reaches Guider, Figuil and Poli.
garoua.angle: Sparse coverage is the whole problem and the whole opening. An agency that registers the North region has very little competition for the orders routed there, and a vendor in Garoua reaches buyers who have almost no local alternative online.

about.metaTitle: About Wi-Mall — built for how Cameroon already sells
about.metaDescription: Wi-Mall is WhatsApp-first commerce for Cameroon: a real catalogue, an assistant that sells inside the chat, and a delivery network of agencies and agents. Why we started, what we believe, and where we actually are.
about.title: Commerce here already runs on WhatsApp. We built the rest.
about.lead: Not a Western storefront translated into French. Wi-Mall is the catalogue, the assistant and the delivery leg that were missing from a market that already works.

why.title: Why we started
why.p1: Open WhatsApp in Douala on any weekday and you will find a market. A seller posts three photos to a status. A buyer replies. They agree a price in the thread, and somebody arranges a moto. It works, and it has worked for years.
why.p2: What does not work is everything around it. The seller is the catalogue, the salesperson and the dispatcher at once, and all three only exist while the phone is in their hand. So the same five questions come back all day. Is it still available. How much. What colours. Do you deliver to my area. Can I pay when it arrives.
why.p3: The usual answer is an app: a download, an account, a password and a card form. That is a lot of steps to buy a phone charger, over a connection that may not survive them — and it asks a working market to move somewhere it never asked to go.
why.p4: So we did not build a place to move to. We built what was missing behind the chat: a real catalogue, an assistant that answers at two in the morning the same way it would at two in the afternoon, a way to take payment both sides trust, and a delivery leg that does not depend on knowing a guy.

how.title: What Wi-Mall actually does
how.lead: Six steps, and a vendor is only involved in the first and the last.
how.s1Body: No download, no account, no password. A WhatsApp message is the whole entry.
how.s2Title: The assistant works out what they want
how.s2Body: It reads intent rather than keywords, and answers in the language the customer wrote in.
how.s3Title: An order is created in the thread
how.s3Body: Confirmed and paid without leaving the conversation.
how.s4Body: It arrives already paid and already addressed, with the delivery fee attached.
how.s5Body: They see the pay before accepting. Tracking is live and confirmation is real.
how.s6Body: Vendor, agency and agent, out of the same completed transaction.

here.title: Why Cameroon first
here.lead: Because the constraints here are the design brief, not an afterthought.
here.p1: Wi-Mall prices in FCFA, speaks French and English, settles through the mobile money people actually use, and organises delivery by region — because that is how the country is organised.
here.p2: Mobile money through MTN, Orange and Moov. Cards for whoever has one. And cash on delivery as a first-class way to pay rather than an awkward exception: collected at the door by the agent, reconciled with their agency, and split exactly the way a card payment would be.
here.p3: It is built for entry-level handsets, expensive data and networks that drop, because here that is the normal case rather than the edge case. All ten regions are in scope. A region with no agency covering it yet is not one Wi-Mall refuses — it is an opening.

foursides.title: Every order pays four sides
foursides.lead: One transaction, four people who each did part of the work.
foursides.vendorBody: Sells without building a storefront, a website or an audience. The catalogue and the assistant do the repeating.
foursides.agencyBody: Receives real shipments with a destination and a fee attached, and splits that fee with its agents.

foursides.note: Wi-Mall takes nothing out of the delivery fee. The platform earns a commission on paid orders, and sells optional plans and credits to the selling side. That is the reason nobody is trying to charge a customer for a chat.

beliefs.title: What we believe
beliefs.lead: Five things that settle arguments here.
beliefs.b1Body: No storefront, app or account should stand between someone and a purchase.
beliefs.b2Body: Discovery, recommendation and ordering happen through conversation, not navigation.
beliefs.b3Title: Every transaction pays all four sides
beliefs.b3Body: Vendor, agency, agent and platform value has to move together, or the arrangement is not working.
beliefs.b4Body: Mobile-dominant, entry-level devices and unreliable networks are the case we design for, not the one we apologise for.
beliefs.b5Body: We are early. Real proof gets presented as proof, and targets get presented as targets.

build.title: How we build
build.lead: Some of this is unusual enough to be worth stating plainly.
build.i1: The build fails if our own marketing copy contradicts the live price list. Prices live in one catalogue, and a page quoting a number that has since changed stops the next deploy and names the line to fix — rather than quietly publishing a page that lies about the price.
build.i2: No invented numbers in structured data. There are no ratings or review counts in our schema markup, because there is no review data yet. The scale figures on this site are first-year targets, and they are labelled as targets.
build.i3: Five languages, including a right-to-left one, from the first line rather than as a later pass.
build.i4: Written for the network people actually have. The words ship inside the HTML, animation is optional, and nothing that matters waits on JavaScript that may never arrive.
build.note: None of that is heroic. It is just what it takes for a page to still be true six months after somebody wrote it.

now.title: Where we are now
now.p1: Early. Real, but early: there are orders and there are users, and there are not many of either yet. We would rather write that down than publish a number we invented.
now.p2: Which is why there are no testimonials on this site, no customer logos and no press quotes. When those exist they will appear here, and they will be real.
now.p3: What there is: a working platform, a free tier that is not a trial, and room for the vendors who arrive first to shape what gets built next.

why.title: What you would be working on
why.p1: Wi-Mall is a WhatsApp-first commerce platform for Cameroon: an assistant that sells inside a chat, a real catalogue behind it, and a network of delivery agencies and agents that gets the thing to a door.
why.p2: The surface is wider than the team. A modular TypeScript backend with its own command bus, a Next.js front end in five languages including a right-to-left one, a mobile app for delivery agents, a separate tracking service, and a payments layer that has to speak mobile money, cards and cash on delivery without treating any of them as the odd one out.
why.p3: That is a lot for the number of people currently doing it. It is the honest pitch, and it is also the interesting part.

how.title: How we work
how.lead: Some of it is unusual. Better to know before you write than after.
how.i1: Correctness is enforced by the build, not by good intentions. Marketing copy that contradicts the live price catalogue fails the deploy and names the line to fix.
how.i2: We do not publish numbers we cannot stand behind. No invented review counts, no fabricated traction, and targets labelled as targets.
how.i3: Africa-first is a constraint we actually honour: entry-level handsets, expensive data, networks that drop. If it only works on fast wifi, it does not work.
how.i4: Comments explain why, not what. A decision that would read as a bug without context gets the context written next to it.
how.i5: Five languages from the start, never as a later pass. Nothing ships English-only.
how.note: If that reads as unnecessary rigour for an early product, this is probably not the right team — and that is a useful thing for both of us to find out early.
